utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-40-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal versus Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll hear the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Myself, Carla Del Ponte, and my colleague, Brenda Hollis, are here for the Prosecution, and Mrs. Javier is also present. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Krstan Simic, and today I represent Mrs. Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the initial appearance of the accused in this case to be conducted in accordance with Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The first matter we have to deal with concerns the indictment and the accused's pleas to it. The accused has the right to have the indictment read out before she pleads to it, but this is a right which she may waive. Mr. Simic, does your client waive the right to have the indictment read out or does she want it read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mrs. Plavsic has received the indictment, studied it. She understands it and there is no need for it to be read out. Therefore, we waive that right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. The next stage is the accused's pleas to the indictment. The Rules provide that the accused must be informed that, within 30 days of today, she will be called on to enter a plea on each of the counts in the indictment. But should the accused so request, she may enter her pleas today. Mr. Simic, two questions for you: First of all, does the accused understand the indictment and the matters to which she has to plead? I understand from your earlier answer that she does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Professor Biljana Plavsic, yesterday, on the 10th of January, 2001, received the indictment which charges her with the crimes described therein. She has read the indictment, understood it; together we have studied it. Mrs. Plavsic has been familiarised with the Rules of Procedure and the Statute of the Tribunal, and she is ready today to enter a plea on the counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Mrs. Plavsic, will you stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Will you confine your answers to "guilty" or "not guilty" to each of the counts as I put them to you. Counts 1 to 6 of the indictment allege offences against Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats, committed between July 1991 and December 1992. In Count 1 of the indictment, you are charged with genocide, punishable under Articles 4(3), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the International Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I received the indictment yesterday, I have understood it fully, and I plead not guilty on all counts of that indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. I must put the counts to you. Count 2, complicity in genocide, punishable under Articles 4, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 3, extermination, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(b), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 4, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 5, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 6, wilful killing, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(a), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 7 charges you with persecution during the same period. The charge is one of persecution on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Counts 8 and 9 charge you with deportation and inhumane acts during the same period. Count 8 charges deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Count 9 charges you with inhumane acts (forced transfer), a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Madam Prosecutor, going on to the next stage of the proceedings, as you know, the Prosecution are required, within 30 days of today, to provide the Defence with copies of the supporting material for the confirmation of this indictment in a language which the accused understands. May I take it that this matter is in hand?

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I can inform you and the Defence attorney can confirm that he has already received all the supporting material with the indictment. To be quite precise, a video is lacking which we will tender in the next few days. Therefore, all the documents except for this video. I also wish to underline that we have provided the documents in two languages, which means including the language of the accused, that is, the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, it seems that disclosure is taking place, has substantially been completed. When it is -- let me remind you that all preliminary motions must be brought within 30 days of Prosecution disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can confirm what the Prosecutor has just said, that yesterday the Office of the Prosecutor disclosed to the Defence a large number of documents. Understandably, however, we have not been able to review those documents and sign a receipt as to all the documents that we have received. We do believe that the disclosure has been accomplished, and as soon as we receive the video cassette, we understand that the time begins to run as envisaged by the Statute and the Rules of Procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are there any other matters which you want Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and the English transcripts. to raise at this hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know whether this is the right place or time, but I would like to highlight a problem which we consider to be a very serious one and it is something that we have already discussed with the Office of the Prosecutor. That is the question of detention. We are not raising the issue of release from detention because we understand the Rules in that regard. However, we believe that the conditions in the Detention Unit which has been designed as a detention unit for men is unacceptable because it is inappropriate for the detention of a woman, in this case Ms. Plavsic. In all prisons in the world, there are separate facilities for men and women. Should an area be appropriately adjusted for Ms. Plavsic, she would still be living in a male environment and, in fact, she would be in absolute isolation, and we all know what that would mean for the accused because solitary detention is punishment and this is something that has not been envisaged in this particular case. So we consider this to be a very serious problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, the matters about detention and the conditions of detention are not matters for the Trial Chamber to determine. They are matters for the President. So if you have any applications in respect of the conditions of detention, you should make them promptly to the President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will do that. It was not our intention to make any requests of the Chamber. We just felt it our duty to inform the Chamber, but we will act in accordance with the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Madam Prosecutor, is there anything that you wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, very briefly. Simply in response to what has been said by the Defence, I should like to underline that we as the Prosecution are fully aware of this problem, and we will try to find a solution which will be in conformity with conditions of detention. But as you know, this is not the place to discuss this. I just wish to inform the Trial Chamber that in a few days time we will submitting a motion for joinder of the indictment of Ms. Plavsic with the indictment of the accused Krajisnik. This is just by way of information for the Trial Chamber. I think that is all we have to raise at this moment. Thank you Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor, you spoke of joinder. Does that mean that there will be a single indictment for both accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have requested a joinder, and we are ready to issue a single indictment, without any judgement, of course, because the facts are virtually the same. So if the Chamber requires us to produce a single indictment, we will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that would be preferable, to issue a single indictment. It would be simpler and more practical for us in terms of procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. If there are no further matters to be raised, this case will be adjourned until the first Status Conference. That must take place before the 11th of May. In due course, we will consider the application for joining this indictment with the indictment in the case of Krajisnik. But meanwhile, the case will be adjourned until a date is fixed by the Trial Chamber or by the Pre-Trial Judge, before the 11th of May. The accused, meanwhile, must remain in the Detention Unit. That concludes this hearing.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Initial Appearance adjourned at
